claims_control: External resource estimates, measured QEC evidence, platform maturity evidence, classical-decoder designs, and vendor roadmaps only; no production key break is claimed. Cross-architecture extrapolation is prohibited without a complete fault-tolerant overhead model, and roadmap/prototype/decoder design evidence is never treated as delivered attack capability.

attack_estimates.name: Google Quantum AI 2026 low-width secp256k1 ECDLP
attack_estimates.runtime_note: Published superconducting scenario says minutes with fewer than 500,000 physical qubits under stated assumptions; no exact runtime is encoded here.

attack_estimates.name: IonQ Walking Cat trapped-ion secp256k1 ECDLP
attack_estimates.runtime_note: 25.7 days per attempt under the published Walking Cat architecture assumptions.

attack_estimates.name: Luo et al. 2026 space-efficient complete ECDLP
attack_estimates.runtime_note: 835 logical qubits is a complete Shor/ECDLP width result. The stored Toffoli value is the 919*n^3/log2(n) leading term evaluated at n=256; the paper also includes O(n^2). Do not infer fast runtime without architecture-specific compilation.

hardware_roadmaps.claims_note: Forward-looking vendor target only. It is 35 logical qubits below the Luo 835-qubit width result; no attack capability is inferred.

Forward-looking vendor target only. The target numerically overlaps IonQ's published Walking Cat attack envelope of 19,397 physical and 1,457 logical qubits. This is a migration-planning trigger, not evidence that the target will be achieved or that the attack will execute as modeled.

platform_maturity_evidence.related_qec_note: IonQ reports breakeven qLDPC QEC on a Tempo engineering test system and describes this as validating key elements of Walking Cat on hardware.
platform_maturity_evidence.claims_note: This raises roadmap maturity above slideware but remains far below the 20,000-physical-qubit attack-scale target and does not establish integrated fault-tolerant cryptanalytic capability.

qec_evidence.name: IonQ breakeven qLDPC demonstration
qec_evidence.claims_note: Demonstrates qLDPC breakeven behavior on trapped-ion hardware. It does not demonstrate the full Walking Cat attack code stack, magic-state factories, 1,457 logical qubits, or attack runtime.

qec_evidence.name: Quantinuum C4-Helix on Helios
qec_evidence.claims_note: Independent trapped-ion evidence that compact logical memory/computation is advancing; no cross-vendor multiplication into an IonQ attack estimate is allowed.

classical_decoder_evidence.name: Generalized qLDPC predecoding architecture
classical_decoder_evidence.evidence_class: proposed classical decoder architecture and hardware design
classical_decoder_evidence.claims_note: This materially reduces the plausibility of classical decoding being an immutable scale bottleneck, but the FPGA/ASIC capacities are design estimates and are not demonstrated as an integrated decoder for IonQ's Walking Cat ECDLP workload.

multi_vendor_fault_tolerance_evidence.finding: Quantinuum reports high-rate logical encoding and fault-tolerant universal-gate/magic-state progress on commercial trapped-ion hardware.
multi_vendor_fault_tolerance_evidence.allowed_use: Independent evidence that fault-tolerant primitives are progressing across more than one trapped-ion vendor; not interchangeable with IonQ's architecture or attack resource estimate.

multi_vendor_fault_tolerance_evidence.finding: Peer-reviewed trapped-ion experiment demonstrates a fault-tolerant universal logical toolbox and a small Grover algorithm on encoded logical qubits.
multi_vendor_fault_tolerance_evidence.allowed_use: Multi-vendor/platform technology-trend evidence only; not proof of cryptanalytic scale.

full_stack_convergence_policy.purpose: Detect when attack-resource estimates, same-architecture roadmaps, prototype/manufacturing progress, QEC hardware evidence, and classical-decoder capacity are converging before a production break exists.
full_stack_convergence_policy.hard_rule: A multi-plane convergence signal may accelerate migration validation but never establishes Q2, Q3, Q4, Q-day, or a demonstrated production break without integrated hardware/runtime evidence.
full_stack_convergence_policy.current_trigger: IonQ's 2028 attack-envelope roadmap collision is now accompanied by fabricated/trapped-ion Superion 256 prototypes, reported breakeven qLDPC on related trapped-ion hardware, and a separate published qLDPC decoder design whose FPGA capacity is near the logical width of the Walking Cat attack estimate. Exact code compatibility and end-to-end integration remain unproven.
